findings.evidence: Configuration or migrations go first when later behavior needs them, not last by category.
findings.fix: Keep the rule; add the non-obvious case a reviewer misses, such as a feature flag or migration that later groups silently depend on, and name the symptom when it is ordered last.

findings.evidence: Group files by purpose (not by directory), one group per reviewable idea.
findings.fix: State the Process pattern's checkpoint: after section 2's manifest recheck passes, and only then, write section 3. The procedure is already there; the phase boundary is not.

findings.evidence: Tool output is truncated beyond roughly 10-30K characters without warning.
findings.fix: Keep the Gotchas. Add one NEVER with a why for the two-dot trap already taught in rule 3: NEVER report an A..B diff as 'only this branch's changes', because git diff A B also shows later commits on A as reversed hunks.

findings.evidence: Not for editing code, a defect-focused code review, or the PR-workflow command explain-pr-changes.
findings.fix: Explain a git diff, commit, branch, range, PR or pasted patch as dependency-ordered logical groups with file references and a review sequence. Use when the user wants to understand, onboard onto or walk through a changeset, asks what changed or what to read first, even without saying 'mental model'. Not for editing the code, a defect-focused review, or the PR-workflow command explain-pr-changes.

findings.evidence: Above roughly 800 changed lines or 30 files, which is where the truncation gotcha below starts to bite, switch to this procedure
findings.fix: Make the threshold one default: above 30 files or 800 changed lines, always page; below both, read the full diff unless a tool result was visibly cut. Drop the 'roughly' and the separate 10-30K gotcha range, or tie that range to the same default.

findings.evidence: Six scenarios cover range order, a missing ref, HEAD~3, custom, an empty diff and a large branch; none is a merge commit.
findings.fix: Add a merge-commit scenario: more than one parent, so git show is empty and the agent must run git diff "<arg>^1" "<arg>" --no-color, with assertions that no combined diff is reported as empty and the manifest uses git diff --name-only between those two revs.

findings.evidence: Verified and it is a branch (`git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/<arg>"` or `refs/remotes/<arg>`): base is the first that exists of `main`, `master`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`
findings.fix: Resolve the branch test for a remote-tracking name: try refs/remotes/<arg> only when <arg> contains a slash, and also try refs/remotes/origin/<arg> for a local-looking name. A name that matches neither, such as origin/feature/x, currently falls through to rule 7 and is explained as one commit.
